audit_findings.title: Parent-only owner earnings are divided by whole-business claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 41.2650 million as-exchanged LLC claims, 38.6% of the 106.9835 million denominator; mechanically removing them while holding equity value unchanged raises base value from $25.18 to approximately $40.99 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: The owner-earnings numerator excludes earnings attributable to noncontrolling LLC interests, while the share denominator includes the Class A shares issuable for those interests.
audit_findings.evidence: The financial position and results of operations attributable to LLC Units we do not own are reported separately as noncontrolling interest.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated numerator-denominator mismatch and is large enough to materially change the per-share valuation. The mechanical $40.99 result is not a corrected valuation because an if-converted calculation must also add the LLC holders' owner earnings and incremental corporate taxes consistently.
audit_findings.action: Rerun either a parent-only valuation using only corresponding Class A claims or an if-converted valuation adding noncontrolling owner earnings and incremental corporate taxes; reconcile every bridge item to the same ownership basis.

audit_findings.title: The denominator assumes exchanges that can create substantial unmodeled TRA claims
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.412 million latest recorded TRA liability, equal to approximately $0.18 per diluted share and 0.7% of the $2.694 billion base equity value; incremental exchange-related TRA is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: TRA obligations are claims on holding-company cash that are not absorbed in equity-level owner earnings and therefore require a bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Future payments to the pre-IPO owners in respect of any subsequent exchanges of LLC Units and Class B common shares for Class A common stock would be in addition to these amounts and are expected to be substantial.
audit_findings.explanation: Omission of the recorded liability is demonstrated but, by itself, would reduce base value only from approximately $25.18 to $25.00 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. The denominator assumes conversion of the remaining LLC interests, however, and the filing says the resulting additional TRA payments are expected to be substantial without providing an amount; materiality of that additional claim remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the June 30, 2026 recorded TRA liability, obtain a tax-basis and TRA schedule for conversion of all 45.885804 million LLC Units, and rerun normal-exchange and accelerated-payment cases.

audit_findings.title: Temporary North Fork income may have been capitalized as perpetual owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $26.108 million pretax filed items comprising $17.632 million of FY2025 development fees and an $8.476 million development gain, equal to 14.3% of the $182.0 million anchor; exact owner-earnings effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: One-time gains, prior-period catch-up revenue and finite development or management fees can inflate the owner-earnings anchor and every forecast and terminal-value period.
audit_findings.evidence: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company recorded $ 17.6 million in development fee revenue and the corresponding receivable, which included a $ 6.1 million cumulative revenue catch-up related to prior years.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the identified income is project-specific and finite, including a $6.1 million prior-period catch-up and a seven-year management term. The record does not show whether the owner-earnings worksheet removed or faded these amounts. If it did not, the identified pretax amount is large enough relative to the anchor to materially overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $182.0 million anchor line by line to remove the $8.476 million gain and $6.1 million catch-up, then rerun development fees only through completion and management fees only over the contractual seven-year term with matched costs and taxes.

audit_findings.title: North Fork carries a large off-balance-sheet completion commitment
audit_findings.magnitude: $425.0 million contractual cap, equal to 233.5% of the $182.0 million anchor and 15.8% of the $2.694 billion base equity value; expected funding and recoverable loss are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A guaranty draw would require cash advances; any unrecoverable portion would reduce the equity bridge or future owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Under the completion guaranty, the Company has agreed to make reimbursable interest-bearing advances to the Mono for completion of the project in the event that total project costs exceed the financing available under the Mono’s facility loan.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitment is filed and potentially large, but funding is contingent, management states it is not probable, and the advances would be reimbursable and interest-bearing. No present loss is established. The active legal challenge, construction risk and subordinated recovery make this a forward-looking exposure requiring monitoring rather than a quantified current deduction.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest project budget, contingency draw schedule, lender reports, federal-litigation status and recovery waterfall; probability-weight guaranty funding and recovery impairment in a rerun if evidence indicates a probable draw.

audit_findings.title: The LLC-unit exchange ratio is a critical denominator dependency
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 valuation adjustment: the 106.9835 million denominator reconciles to 59.130385 million Class A shares plus 45.885804 million LLC Units at the computed June 30, 2026 ratio of 0.899297, plus 5.377764 million options and 1.210386 million restricted shares
audit_findings.mechanism: The exchange ratio determines the Class A-equivalent shares contributed by LLC Units to the fully diluted denominator.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the exchange ratio was 0.908 shares of Class A common stock for each LLC Unit and share of Class B common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The dependency is real, but the supplied denominator did not treat the LLC Units one-for-one. It applies the June 30 ratio computed from 59.130385 million Class A shares divided by 65.751788 million Red Rock-owned LLC Units and therefore needs no adjustment. This does not resolve the separate numerator-basis error in finding 1.
audit_findings.action: Retain the denominator but document the 0.899297 ratio and its reconciliation; update it whenever Class A shares or Red Rock-owned LLC Units change.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method earnings may lack matched reinvestment deductions
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.606 million of FY2025 joint-venture earnings, equal to 1.4% of the $182.0 million anchor; distributions, maintenance capital and financing obligations are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method income can enter owner earnings without the investees' maintenance capital expenditures or distributable-cash limitations appearing in the consolidated cash-flow statement.
audit_findings.evidence: Investments in all 50 % or less owned affiliated companies are accounted for using the equity method.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates inclusion of $2.606 million of joint-venture earnings, but the record does not establish whether the owner-earnings worksheet substituted cash distributions or deducted the company's share of maintenance reinvestment. The known earnings amount is small relative to the anchor, but unreported investee capital and financing requirements prevent a supported materiality conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 equity-method income to cash distributions and obtain investee cash-flow statements, maintenance capital expenditures, debt service and guarantees; rerun owner earnings using sustainable distributable cash.
